producer_report.summary: A check killed at its deadline now ends the job as an environment stop that `athena retry` resumes, instead of a rejection. `athena status` also reports test-check durations. All three parts are in this job. The targeted tests, clippy and the policy scan passed. The full `cargo test --locked` run returned without an error, but I could not read its summary (see open_issues). Root cause: a kill at the deadline was stored like a real failure (exit code None, not passed), so `judge` rejected the job, as in job 20261026-232434-6wfq. (1) `athena.toml` check_timeout_s is 1800; config.rs is untouched. (2) checks.rs gains `deadline_note` (the one text `run_check` writes and the classifier reads), `timed_out(&CheckRun)` and `held_for_timeout(&[CheckRun], Option<&Baseline>)`. It looks only at new failures, meaning failed and not pre-existing on the base, and returns the longest timed-out check only when there is at least one and all of them timed out. A real failure beside a timeout is not held, so it is rejected as before. (3) disk.rs gains `CHECK_TIMEOUT` ("environment: check timed out") and `check_timeout_reason`, which prints e.g. '905s of 900s limit' and the retry command. `is_environment_reason` accepts the new reason, so `resumable_stop` follows. (4) In `check_and_verify`, right after `mark_pre_existing`, a held job closes through `self.failure` before the verifier, as the low-disk stop does. A cfg(test) `check_seam` module in run/mod.rs, read first in `SnapExec::exec`, lets tests supply a killed-at-deadline result. (5) status.rs gains `CheckDurations` and `check_durations()`: median and slowest of the `test` check over the newest 20 jobs with a measured run, 'not run' placeholders excluded, flagged above 80% of check_timeout_s. The field `check_durations` is in `StatusView` and `--json`. (6) display.rs prints it as a `checks     test:` line. (7) CHANGELOG.md has an Unreleased entry citing job 20261026-232434-6wfq.

checks_run.command: cargo test --locked -p athena-core -- a_check_killed_at_its_deadline a_real_nonzero_check held_for_timeout a_real_deadline_kill only_a_deadline_kill the_longest_timed_out the_check_timeout_reason check_timeout_reason check_durations

crates/athena-cli/src/display.rs is not in the brief's expected deliverables. I changed it (a 3-line `if let` in `status()`) because it is the only code that prints StatusView, so `athena status` would not show the report without it. It is not a governance file.

I added crates/athena-cli/tests/status_durations.rs (new), which the brief does not list. It is the display-level test `status_prints_the_check_durations_line`. I used an integration test instead of a unit test in display.rs because the unit tests there have no way to build a StatusView. It seeds verification records in a fixture repo and checks `display::status` output.

A held job writes no check record, so its duration appears only in the closing reason and never in the status report. The jobs closest to the limit are the ones most likely to be missing. This was accepted in the reading and follows the low-disk stop.

Follow-up: code_health::suite_seconds (code_health.rs) takes the latest `test` duration without excluding 'not run' placeholders, so it can report 0 s. A one-line fix is to apply the same basis filter as `test_check_seconds` in status.rs. I left it alone because code_health.rs is not a deliverable.
A genuinely hung check is now held as an environment stop rather than rejected. The job needs a manual `athena retry`, and `athena status` flags a slowest run above 80% of the limit.
mistakes: In the first edit I wrote a hacky marker built by trimming `deadline_note(0)`. I replaced it with a `DEADLINE_NOTE_START` constant before testing.
I ran `cargo test --locked` before checking how its output would be reported, so its summary was lost to an unreadable saved file. I did not re-run, since the brief allows one full run.
learnings: The harness takes a baseline on the base commit with real processes. A test check that always fails (such as `false`) is therefore pre-existing and would not reject the job. The existing FAILS_ON_EDIT check (passes on the base, fails after the edit) is the right fixture for a real failure.

routing::run_local stops at the first failed check, so a local run never produces a mixed set of failures. Mixed sets come only from reused CI records, which is why the mixed case is tested on `held_for_timeout` directly.
mark_pre_existing only prefixes the note and `is_pre_existing` depends only on `passed` and the baseline. A 'contains' match for the deadline note therefore still works after marking.
Bash in this environment blocks `tail`, and Read/Grep block files outside the working directory, including the saved overflow output of a large cargo run.
